title: stream sentinel resolution and tool output shaping for v1/chat.completions parity
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Close remaining parity gaps between Redwood's /v1/chat.completions adapter and OpenAI semantics around stop heuristics, streaming sentinel resolution, and function/tool output shaping. Users observed edge cases where: 1) stream fragments could emit duplicate sentinel indicators (partial stop tokens) leading to downstream parsers seeing multiple 'stop' events; 2) function/tool responses in framed JSON envelopes did not always include the canonical metadata keys OpenAI clients expect (name, arguments, parsed_args) causing client-side deserialization errors; 3) logprob reconciliation for partial deltas produced inconsistent scores for final tokens when stop tokens were synthesized by the adapter.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a deterministic sentinel coalescer for stream fragments, upgrades the framed JSON tool envelope to include a stable signature and secondary metadata fields for backwards compatibility, and normalizes logprob fallback logic so token-level probabilities agree with the non-streaming path. The changes are additive and gated under the existing v1 adapter flag; default behavior for customers is unchanged unless they opt into the stricter OpenAI-parity mode via the compatibility toggle.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stream sentinel coalescer that merges adjacent partial stop deltas into a single sentinel emission
- [x] Ensure final chunk emits a single canonical stop event with normalized index mapping
- [x] Extend toolcall envelope: include "tool_name", "tool_args_raw", "tool_args_parsed" and keep legacy "name"/"arguments" keys for older clients
- [x] Reconcile streaming logprob deltas with batch logprob computation for identical prompt+model seed
- [x] Add unit tests for parser edge cases and an end-to-end e2e test using mock client
- [x] Update docs/openai_compat.md with expected framed envelope shape and migration notes

Compatibility/rollback: All code paths are behind the v1 compatibility toggle. If downstream issues are reported, ops can flip the adapter flag to revert to prior behavior without restarting serving instances. No customer-visible new API surface; only response envelope additions (backwards compatible).

Testing performed: Local unit tests, e2e harness with mock OpenAI client, CI run (lint, go tests, python sdk smoke) — CI initially failed on a flaky fragment test which was fixed by increasing inter-fragment buffer tolerance and adding a strict coalescer test. See commits for details.
commits: coalesce: add stream sentinel coalescer and unit tests
compat: extend tool envelope with legacy and stabilized keys
logprob: introduce streaming->batch reconciliation path and tests
docs: document framed tool envelope and migration guide
review_thread: Diego Martinez: I like the sentinel coalescer but can you add a short comment describing why we choose to merge on byte-boundary vs token-boundary? (clients observed UTF-8 split edgecases)
Asha Patel: Added explanation + a test that fakes UTF-8 split fragments to ensure we don't generate invalid JSON. See coalescer_test.go: TestUtf8SplitSentinel

Karen Li: The tool envelope change is safe, but we should preserve exact key names for legacy clients. Suggest keeping both "arguments" and "tool_args_raw". Also request a changelog entry for the SDK team.
Asha Patel: Preserved legacy keys and added the SDK smoke test. Changelog note added to docs/openai_compat.md under Migration -> SDK updates.
Omar Rahman: Observed a small perf regression on the canary (p95 token latency +1.8ms). Can we micro-opt the coalescer to avoid extra allocations?
Asha Patel: Optimized buffer reuse in coalescer (replaced a temporary slice allocation with a pooled buffer). Re-ran canary, p95 delta reduced to +0.4ms and accepted.
Diego Martinez: Approving after Buffer reuse optimization and test green. +1
release_notes: Stabilize v1/chat.completions parity for streaming: coalesces stream sentinels to avoid duplicate stop events, adds backward-compatible tool call envelope fields (tool_name/tool_args_raw/tool_args_parsed), and aligns streaming logprob deltas with batch logprob computation. Opt-in under v1 compatibility flag. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Adapter toggle: compatibility.v1.openai_parity = true to enable. Rolling restart not required; flip flag in control plane. Monitor metric: compat.stream.sentinel_coalesced_count and compat.logprob.reconciliation_errors.
qa_notes: Add the provided e2e test to nightly regression suite. Watch for regressions in tests/e2e/chat_stop_parity_test.go. If CI shows intermittent fragment timing failures, increase STREAM_FRAGMENT_TIMEOUT in test harness.
impact_statement: No breaking API changes. Minor p95 token latency impact mitigated by buffer pooling. Recommended to enable on staging before production rollouts.
repro_steps: 1) Enable v1 parity toggle in local env. 2) Run tests/e2e/chat_stop_parity_test.go against mock client that splits stop tokens across fragments. 3) Validate single stop event emitted and tool envelope contains both legacy and new keys.
